sanskrit: vīkṣamāṇas tu mandāsuḥ sarvato mandam ucchvasan ādāv eva tu sugrīvaṃ dadarśa tv ātmajāgrataḥ
english: Breathing faintly and gazing all around, Vālī, his life-breath now slow, saw Sugrīva standing there first of all, alert and watchful near his own son.

sanskrit: taṃ prāptavijayaṃ vālī sugrīvaṃ plavageśvaram ābhāṣya vyaktayā vācā sasneham idam abravīt
english: Vālī addressed Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, who had now attained victory, and spoke these words to him with a clear voice full of affection.

sanskrit: sugrīvadoṣeṇa na māṃ gantum arhasi kilbiṣāt kṛṣyamāṇaṃ bhaviṣyeṇa buddhimohena māṃ balāt
english: Do not go blaming Sugrīva's fault for my ruin; it was I who was dragged by force into this, my intellect bewildered by what fate had decreed.

sanskrit: yugapadvihitaṃ tāta na manye sukham āvayoḥ sauhārdaṃ bhrātṛyuktaṃ hi tad idaṃ jātam anyathā
english: Dear brother, I do not think prosperity was ordained for both of us simultaneously; the fraternal bond and affection between us has thus turned out otherwise.

sanskrit: pratipadya tvam adyaiva rājyam eṣāṃ vanaukasām mām apy adyaiva gacchantaṃ viddhi vaivasvatakṣayam
english: Take up at once this very day the kingdom of these forest-dwellers; and know that I too am departing this very day to the abode of Vaivasvata, the god of death.

sanskrit: jīvitaṃ ca hi rājyaṃ ca śriyaṃ ca vipulām imām prajahāmy eṣa vai tūrṇaṃ mahac cāgarhitaṃ yaśaḥ
english: Life, kingdom, this vast royal glory, and great unblemished fame — I am quickly relinquishing all of them now.

sanskrit: asyāṃ tv aham avasthāyāṃ vīra vakṣyāmi yad vacaḥ yady apy asukaraṃ rājan kartum eva tad arhasi
english: O hero, O king, in this condition I shall speak words which, though difficult to carry out, you must nonetheless perform.

sanskrit: sukhārhaṃ sukhasaṃvṛddhaṃ bālam enam abāliśam bāṣpapūrṇamukhaṃ paśya bhūmau patitam aṅgadam
english: Look at this boy Aṅgada, fallen to the ground, his face filled with tears — he who deserves happiness and was reared in comfort, blameless though young.

sanskrit: mama prāṇaiḥ priyataraṃ putraṃ putram ivaurasaṃ mayā hīnam ahīnārthaṃ sarvataḥ paripālaya
english: Guard this son, dearer to me than my own life, as if he were your own born son; though bereft of me, let him lack nothing — protect him in every way.

sanskrit: tvam apy asya hi dātā ca paritrātā ca sarvataḥ bhayeṣv abhayadaś caiva yathāhaṃ plavageśvara
english: You too shall be his provider, his protector in all things, and his deliverer from every fear — just as I was, O lord of the monkeys.

sanskrit: eṣa tārātmajaḥ śrīmāṃs tvayā tulyaparākramaḥ rakṣasāṃ tu vadhe teṣām agratas te bhaviṣyati
english: This glorious son of Tārā, equal to you in valor, shall march at the forefront of your forces in the slaying of those rākṣasas.

sanskrit: anurūpāṇi karmāṇi vikramya balavān raṇe kariṣyaty eṣa tāreyas tarasvī taruṇo 'ṅgadaḥ
english: Young Aṅgada, Tārā's son, swift and mighty, shall perform deeds worthy of his lineage, displaying his prowess in battle.

sanskrit: suṣeṇaduhitā ceyam arthasūkṣmaviniścaye autpātike ca vividhe sarvataḥ pariniṣṭhitā
english: And this daughter of Suṣeṇa — Tārā — is thoroughly versed in adjudicating subtle matters of policy, and is fully accomplished in interpreting all manner of omens and portents.

sanskrit: yad eṣā sādhv iti brūyāt kāryaṃ tan muktasaṃśayam na hi tārāmataṃ kiṃ cid anyathā parivartate
english: Whatever she pronounces as right and proper, let that be done without doubt; for nothing that Tārā deems wise ever turns out otherwise.

sanskrit: rāghavasya ca te kāryaṃ kartavyam aviśaṅkayā syād adharmo hy akaraṇe tvāṃ ca hiṃsyād vimānitaḥ
english: And you must carry out Rāghava's purpose without hesitation; for neglecting it would be unrighteous, and he, if slighted, would harm you.

sanskrit: imāṃ ca mālām ādhatsva divyāṃ sugrīvakāñcanīm udārā śrīḥ sthitā hy asyāṃ saṃprajahyān mṛte mayi
english: And take this divine golden garland of Sugrīva's — great sovereignty resides in it; it would abandon this world on my death.

sanskrit: ity evam uktaḥ sugrīvo vālinā bhrātṛsauhṛdāt harṣaṃ tyaktvā punar dīno grahagrasta ivoḍurāṭ
english: Thus spoken to by Vālī out of brotherly love, Sugrīva, abandoning all joy, became wretched again — like the moon seized by a planet.

sanskrit: tad vālivacanāc chāntaḥ kurvan yuktam atandritaḥ jagrāha so 'bhyanujñāto mālāṃ tāṃ caiva kāñcanīm
english: Pacified by Vālī's words, acting rightly and without hesitation, he accepted — having been given leave — that golden garland.

sanskrit: tāṃ mālāṃ kāñcanīṃ dattvā vālī dṛṣṭvātmajaṃ sthitam saṃsiddhaḥ pretya bhāvāya snehād aṅgadam abravīt
english: Having given away that golden garland and seeing his son standing near, Vālī, readied now for departure from this life, spoke to Aṅgada with affection.

sanskrit: deśakālau bhajasvādya kṣamamāṇaḥ priyāpriye sukhaduḥkhasahaḥ kāle sugrīvavaśago bhava
english: Attend now to place and time; bear with equanimity both the pleasant and the unpleasant; endure joy and sorrow alike; and in due season remain submissive to Sugrīva.

sanskrit: yathā hi tvaṃ mahābāho lālitaḥ satataṃ mayā na tathā vartamānaṃ tvāṃ sugrīvo bahu maṃsyate
english: O mighty-armed one, Sugrīva will not hold you in the same regard as I always did when I indulged you; behave accordingly.

sanskrit: māsyāmitrair gataṃ gaccher mā śatrubhir ariṃdama bhartur arthaparo dāntaḥ sugrīvavaśago bhava
english: Do not follow those who have gone over to enemies; do not go with your foes, O subduer of foes; be self-restrained, devoted to your lord's interests, and obedient to Sugrīva.

sanskrit: na cātipraṇayaḥ kāryaḥ kartavyo 'praṇayaś ca te ubhayaṃ hi mahādoṣaṃ tasmād antaradṛg bhava
english: Neither excessive intimacy nor excessive aloofness should be practiced by you; both are great faults. Therefore be one who sees the middle path.

sanskrit: ity uktvātha vivṛttākṣaḥ śarasaṃpīḍito bhṛśam vivṛtair daśanair bhīmair babhūvotkrāntajīvitaḥ
english: Having said these words, his eyes rolled back, tormented greatly by the arrow, his fearsome teeth bared — Vālī's life departed from him.

sanskrit: hate tu vīre plavagādhipe tadā plavaṃgamās tatra na śarma lebhire vanecarāḥ siṃhayute mahāvane yathā hi gāvo nihate gavāṃ patau
english: When that heroic lord of monkeys was slain, the forest-roaming monkeys found no peace — even as cows in a great forest find no peace when their bull has been killed by a lion.

sanskrit: tatas tu tārā vyasanārṇava plutā mṛtasyā bhartur vadanaṃ samīkṣya sā jagāma bhūmiṃ parirabhya vālinaṃ mahādrumaṃ chinnam ivāśritā latā
english: Then Tārā, overwhelmed and drowned in an ocean of grief, gazed upon the face of her dead husband and fell to the ground embracing Vālī — like a creeper clinging to a great tree that has been felled.

sanskrit: tataḥ samupajighrantī kapirājasya tanmukham patiṃ lokāc cyutaṃ tārā mṛtaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then Tārā, pressing her face close to inhale the scent of the monkey-king's face, her husband fallen from the living world, spoke these words to him as he lay dead.

sanskrit: śeṣe tvaṃ viṣame duḥkham akṛtvā vacanaṃ mama upalopacite vīra suduḥkhe vasudhātale
english: You lie here, O hero, on this hard and painful earth strewn with crushed grass, without having heeded my words — and in great sorrow do I find myself.

sanskrit: mattaḥ priyatarā nūnaṃ vānarendra mahī tava śeṣe hi tāṃ pariṣvajya māṃ ca na pratibhāṣase
english: The earth is surely dearer to you than I am, O lord of monkeys; for you lie there embracing her, and you do not speak a word to me.

sanskrit: sugrīva eva vikrānto vīra sāhasika priya ṛkṣavānaramukhyās tvāṃ balinaṃ paryupāsate
english: O hero, O bold and beloved one — it is Sugrīva alone who has triumphed; yet the chieftains of bears and monkeys attend upon you, the mighty one.

sanskrit: eṣāṃ vilapitaṃ kṛcchram aṅgadasya ca śocataḥ mama cemāṃ giraṃ śrutvā kiṃ tvaṃ na pratibudhyase
english: Hearing the anguished lamentations of these, the grief of sorrowing Aṅgada, and this speech of mine — why do you not wake and reply?

sanskrit: idaṃ tac chūraśayanaṃ yatra śeṣe hato yudhi śāyitā nihatā yatra tvayaiva ripavaḥ purā
english: This is that hero's resting place where you lie slain in battle — the very ground where in former times your enemies were laid low and slaughtered by you.

sanskrit: viśuddhasattvābhijana priyayuddha mama priya mām anāthāṃ vihāyaikāṃ gatas tvam asi mānada
english: O you of pure nature and noble lineage, O lover of battle, my beloved, O giver of honor — you have gone, leaving me alone, without a protector.

sanskrit: śūrāya na pradātavyā kanyā khalu vipaścitā śūrabhāryāṃ hatāṃ paśya sadyo māṃ vidhavāṃ kṛtām
english: Truly the wise should not give a maiden in marriage to a hero; look at the wife of a hero now slain — see me, made a widow in an instant.

sanskrit: avabhagnaś ca me māno bhagnā me śāśvatī gatiḥ agādhe ca nimagnāsmi vipule śokasāgare
english: My pride is shattered; my eternal path is broken; I am sunk deep in a boundless, fathomless ocean of grief.

sanskrit: aśmasāramayaṃ nūnam idaṃ me hṛdayaṃ dṛḍham bhartāraṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā yan nādya śatadhā gatam
english: My heart must surely be made of the hardest iron, for upon seeing my husband slain it does not break into a hundred pieces this very moment.

sanskrit: suhṛc caiva hi bhartā ca prakṛtyā ca mama priyaḥ āhave ca parākrāntaḥ śūraḥ pañcatvam āgataḥ
english: He was my friend, my husband, by nature my beloved; and he was a hero who showed his valor in battle — and now he has merged into the five elements.

sanskrit: patihīnā tu yā nārī kāmaṃ bhavatu putriṇī dhanadhānyaiḥ supūrṇāpi vidhavety ucyate budhaiḥ
english: A woman bereft of her husband — let her have sons if she will, let her be filled with wealth and grain — is still called a widow by the wise.

sanskrit: svagātraprabhave vīra śeṣe rudhiramaṇḍale kṛmirāgaparistome tvam evaṃ śayane yathā
english: O hero, you lie thus on a bed born of your own body — a pool of blood, covered with insects and reddish matter — as if resting on a couch.

sanskrit: reṇuśoṇitasaṃvītaṃ gātraṃ tava samantataḥ parirabdhuṃ na śaknomi bhujābhyāṃ plavagarṣabha
english: Your body is smeared all over with dust and blood; I am unable to embrace it with my arms, O bull among monkeys.

sanskrit: kṛtakṛtyo 'dya sugrīvo vaire 'sminn atidāruṇe yasya rāmavimuktena hṛtam ekeṣuṇā bhayam
english: Sugrīva has today accomplished his purpose in this most terrible enmity — his fear has been removed by a single arrow released by Rāma.

sanskrit: śareṇa hṛdi lagnena gātrasaṃsparśane tava vāryāmi tvāṃ nirīkṣantī tvayi pañcatvam āgate
english: The arrow lodged in your heart prevents me from touching your body; I look at you and hold myself back — now that you have merged into the five elements.

sanskrit: udbabarha śaraṃ nīlas tasya gātragataṃ tadā girigahvarasaṃlīnaṃ dīptam āśīviṣaṃ yathā
english: Then Nīla drew out the arrow lodged in his body — as one draws out a blazing venomous serpent that has coiled itself deep in a mountain cave.

sanskrit: tasya niṣkṛṣyamāṇasya bāṇasya ca babhau dyutiḥ astamastakasaṃruddho raśmir dinakarād iva
english: As that arrow was being drawn out, its radiance shone forth — like a ray of sunlight blocked by the summit of the setting mountain.

sanskrit: petuḥ kṣatajadhārās tu vraṇebhyas tasya sarvaśaḥ tāmragairikasaṃpṛktā dhārā iva dharādharāt
english: Streams of blood poured from his wounds on all sides — like streams tinged with red ochre flowing from a mountain.

sanskrit: avakīrṇaṃ vimārjantī bhartāraṃ raṇareṇunā asrair nayanajaiḥ śūraṃ siṣecāstrasamāhatam
english: Wiping the battle-dust that had settled on her husband, she bathed the hero — struck down by the weapon — with the tears flowing from her eyes.

sanskrit: rudhirokṣitasarvāṅgaṃ dṛṣṭvā vinihataṃ patim uvāca tārā piṅgākṣaṃ putram aṅgadam aṅganā
english: Seeing her husband slain, his entire body drenched in blood, Tārā spoke to her tawny-eyed son Aṅgada.

sanskrit: avasthāṃ paścimāṃ paśya pituḥ putra sudāruṇām saṃprasaktasya vairasya gato 'ntaḥ pāpakarmaṇā
english: Son, look upon the dreadful final condition of your father — one who pursued enmity and met his end through sinful deeds.

sanskrit: bālasūryodayatanuṃ prayāntaṃ yamasādanam abhivādaya rājānaṃ pitaraṃ putra mānadam
english: Son, pay homage to the king your father — who gave honor to all — as he departs to Yama's abode, his body glowing like the rising morning sun.

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ samutthāya jagrāha caraṇau pituḥ bhujābhyāṃ pīnavṛtābhyām aṅgado 'ham iti bruvan
english: Thus addressed, Aṅgada rose up and clasped his father's feet with his two stout rounded arms, saying "I am here, I am Aṅgada."

sanskrit: abhivādayamānaṃ tvām aṅgadaṃ tvaṃ yathāpurā dīrghāyur bhava putreti kimarthaṃ nābhibhāṣase
english: Why do you not speak to Aṅgada as he salutes you — as you used to do before — saying "May you live long, my son"?

sanskrit: ahaṃ putrasahāyā tvām upāse gatacetanam siṃhena nihataṃ sadyo gauḥ savatseva govṛṣam
english: I attend upon you, senseless as you are, together with your son — even as a cow with her calf attends upon a bull that a lion has just slain.

sanskrit: iṣṭvā saṃgrāmayajñena nānāpraharaṇāmbhasā asminn avabhṛthe snātaḥ kathaṃ patnyā mayā vinā
english: Having performed the sacrifice of battle with the waters of various weapons, how did you bathe in this concluding ablution without me, your wife?

sanskrit: yā dattā devarājena tava tuṣṭena saṃyuge śātakumbhamayīṃ mālāṃ tāṃ te paśyāmi neha kim
english: The golden garland that the king of the gods, pleased with you in battle, once gave to you — why do I not see it on you here now?

sanskrit: rājaśrīr na jahāti tvāṃ gatāsum api mānada sūryasyāvartamānasya śailarājam iva prabhā
english: The royal glory does not abandon you even in death, O giver of honor — like the light that does not leave the king of mountains even as the sun moves away.

sanskrit: na me vacaḥ pathyam idaṃ tvayā kṛtaṃ na cāsmi śaktā hi nivāraṇe tava hatā saputrāsmi hatena saṃyuge saha tvayā śrīr vijahāti mām iha
english: You did not heed my wholesome words, nor was I able to restrain you. I am ruined — I and my son — by you who are ruined; along with you slain in battle, prosperity deserts me here.

sanskrit: gatāsuṃ vālinaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāghavas tadanantaram abravīt praśritaṃ vākyaṃ sugrīvaṃ śatrutāpanaḥ
english: Seeing Vālī now lifeless, Rāghava, the scorcher of enemies, thereupon addressed Sugrīva with gentle words.

sanskrit: na śokaparitāpena śreyasā yujyate mṛtaḥ yad atrānantaraṃ kāryaṃ tat samādhātum arhatha
english: The dead are not served by the torment of grief; you should now attend to what is to be done next in this matter.

sanskrit: lokavṛttam anuṣṭheyaṃ kṛtaṃ vo bāṣpamokṣaṇam na kālād uttaraṃ kiṃ cit karma śakyam upāsitum
english: The shedding of tears, which is the way of the world, has been done by you; no act can be carried out beyond its appointed time.

sanskrit: niyataḥ kāraṇaṃ loke niyatiḥ karmasādhanam niyatiḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ niyogeṣv iha kāraṇam
english: Fate is the cause in this world; fate is the instrument of action; fate is the cause that ordains all beings to their appointed tasks here.

sanskrit: na kartā kasya cit kaś cin niyoge cāpi neśvaraḥ svabhāve vartate lokas tasya kālaḥ parāyaṇam
english: No one is the independent maker of anything, nor is anyone master of their own ordainment; the world moves according to its own nature, and time is its ultimate refuge.

sanskrit: na kālaḥ kālam atyeti na kālaḥ parihīyate svabhāvaṃ vā samāsādya na kaś cid ativartate
english: Time does not transcend time; time is never diminished; and once one's nature is reached, no one can transgress it.

sanskrit: na kālasyāsti bandhutvaṃ na hetur na parākramaḥ na mitrajñātisaṃbandhaḥ kāraṇaṃ nātmano vaśaḥ
english: Time has no kinship, no motive, no heroic valor; neither friendship, nor relation, nor family ties are a cause for it; and one's own will is not the cause either.

sanskrit: kiṃ tu kāla parīṇāmo draṣṭavyaḥ sādhu paśyatā dharmaś cārthaś ca kāmaś ca kālakramasamāhitāḥ
english: Rather, the ripening of time must be observed by one who sees clearly; dharma, artha, and kāma are all gathered together through the orderly course of time.

sanskrit: itaḥ svāṃ prakṛtiṃ vālī gataḥ prāptaḥ kriyāphalam dharmārthakāmasaṃyogaiḥ pavitraṃ plavageśvara
english: From here Vālī has gone to his own elemental nature, having attained the fruit of his deeds; he is purified by the conjunction of dharma, artha, and kāma, O lord of monkeys.

sanskrit: svadharmasya ca saṃyogāj jitas tena mahātmanā svargaḥ parigṛhītaś ca prāṇān aparirakṣatā
english: Through his adherence to his own duty, that great soul has conquered and secured heaven — he who did not protect his life in battle.

sanskrit: eṣā vai niyatiḥ śreṣṭhā yāṃ gato hariyūthapaḥ tad alaṃ paritāpena prāptakālam upāsyatām
english: This is indeed the highest destiny that this leader of monkey troops has attained; therefore enough with grief — let what is timely and appropriate now be attended to.

sanskrit: vacanānte tu rāmasya lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā avadat praśritaṃ vākyaṃ sugrīvaṃ gatacetasaṃ
english: When Rāma had finished speaking, Lakṣmaṇa, the slayer of enemy heroes, addressed Sugrīva, who was lost in grief, with gentle words.

sanskrit: kuru tvam asya sugrīva pretakāryam anantaram tārāṅgadābhyāṃ sahito vālino dahanaṃ prati
english: Sugrīva, perform the funeral rites for him now without delay; together with Tārā and Aṅgada, proceed with the cremation of Vālī.

sanskrit: samājñāpaya kāṣṭhāni śuṣkāṇi ca bahūni ca candanāni ca divyāni vālisaṃskārakāraṇāt
english: Give orders for many dry pieces of wood to be assembled, along with divine sandalwood — for the purpose of Vālī's obsequies.

sanskrit: samāśvāsaya cainaṃ tvam aṅgadaṃ dīnacetasaṃ mā bhūr bāliśabuddhis tvaṃ tvadadhīnam idaṃ puram
english: Comfort Aṅgada whose heart is stricken; do not be foolish in your thinking — this city now depends upon you.

sanskrit: aṅgadas tv ānayen mālyaṃ vastrāṇi vividhāni ca ghṛtaṃ tailam atho gandhān yac cātra samanantaram
english: Let Aṅgada bring garlands, various garments, clarified butter, oil, perfumes, and whatever else is required next in this matter.

sanskrit: tvaṃ tāra śibikāṃ śīghram ādāyāgaccha saṃbhramāt tvarā guṇavatī yuktā hy asmin kāle viśeṣataḥ
english: You, Tāra, quickly bring a palanquin with all haste; speed is especially meritorious at this particular time.

sanskrit: sajjībhavantu plavagāḥ śibikāvāhanocitāḥ samarthā balinaś caiva nirhariṣyanti vālinam
english: Let the monkeys who are fit to bear a palanquin make themselves ready — those who are capable and strong — they shall carry Vālī forth.

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu sugrīvaṃ sumitrānandavardhanaḥ tasthau bhrātṛsamīpastho lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā
english: Having spoken thus to Sugrīva, Lakṣmaṇa — increaser of Sumitrā's joy, slayer of enemy heroes — stood by his brother's side.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā tāraḥ saṃbhrāntamānasaḥ praviveśa guhāṃ śīghraṃ śibikāsaktamānasaḥ
english: Hearing Lakṣmaṇa's words, Tāra, his mind agitated and his thoughts fixed on the palanquin, quickly entered the cave.

sanskrit: ādāya śibikāṃ tāraḥ sa tu paryāpayat punaḥ vānarair uhyamānāṃ tāṃ śūrair udvahanocitaiḥ
english: Taking the palanquin, Tāra furnished it duly, to be borne by monkeys — those heroic ones trained to carry burdens.

sanskrit: tato vālinam udyamya sugrīvaḥ śibikāṃ tadā āropayata vikrośann aṅgadena sahaiva tu
english: Then Sugrīva, lifting Vālī and wailing aloud, placed him upon the palanquin — together with Aṅgada.

sanskrit: āropya śibikāṃ caiva vālinaṃ gatajīvitam alaṃkāraiś ca vividhair mālyair vastraiś ca bhūṣitam
english: Having placed Vālī, bereft of life, upon the palanquin, he was adorned with various ornaments, garlands, and garments.

sanskrit: ājñāpayat tadā rājā sugrīvaḥ plavageśvaraḥ aurdhvadehikam āryasya kriyatām anurūpataḥ
english: Then King Sugrīva, lord of monkeys, gave command: "Let the post-mortem rites befitting a noble one be performed duly."

sanskrit: viśrāṇayanto ratnāni vividhāni bahūni ca agrataḥ plavagā yāntu śibikā tadanantaram
english: "Let the monkeys go in front, distributing various gems in great numbers; the palanquin shall follow directly after."

sanskrit: rājñām ṛddhiviśeṣā hi dṛśyante bhuvi yādṛśāḥ tādṛśaṃ vālinaḥ kṣipraṃ prākurvann aurdhvadehikam
english: Such special royal splendors as are seen among kings on earth — with such did they swiftly perform Vālī's post-mortem rites.

sanskrit: aṅgadam aprigṛhyāśu tāraprabhṛtayas tathā krośantaḥ prayayuḥ sarve vānarā hatabāndhavāḥ
english: Quickly taking hold of Aṅgada, and together with Tāra and the others, all the monkeys, bereaved of their kinsman, went forward weeping aloud.

sanskrit: tārāprabhṛtayaḥ sarvā vānaryo hatayūthapāḥ anujagmur hi bhartāraṃ krośantyaḥ karuṇasvanāḥ
english: All the female monkeys, led by Tārā, whose troop-leader had been slain, followed their husband with piteous cries, wailing mournfully.

sanskrit: tāsāṃ ruditaśabdena vānarīṇāṃ vanāntare vanāni girayaś ca sarve vikrośantīva sarvataḥ
english: By the sound of those female monkeys weeping in the forest's depths, the forests and all the mountains seemed to cry out in every direction.

sanskrit: puline girinadyās tu vivikte jalasaṃvṛte citāṃ cakruḥ subahavo vānarā vanacāriṇaḥ
english: On a sandbar of a mountain river, in a secluded place surrounded by water, the many forest-roaming monkeys built the funeral pyre.

sanskrit: avaropya tataḥ skandhāc chibikāṃ vahanocitāḥ tasthur ekāntam āśritya sarve śokasamanvitāḥ
english: Then those trained to carry, lowering the palanquin from their shoulders, stood apart in a secluded spot, all overcome with grief.

sanskrit: tatas tārā patiṃ dṛṣṭvā śibikātalaśāyinam āropyāṅke śiras tasya vilalāpa suduḥkhitā
english: Then Tārā, seeing her husband lying on the floor of the palanquin, placed his head in her lap and lamented in profound sorrow.

sanskrit: janaṃ ca paśyasīmaṃ tvaṃ kasmāc chokābhipīḍitam prahṛṣṭam iva te vaktraṃ gatāsor api mānada astārkasamavarṇaṃ ca lakṣyate jīvato yathā
english: You seem to look upon this grief-stricken people — your face appears almost joyful, O giver of honor; even in death it glows like the color of the setting sun, as though you still lived.

sanskrit: eṣa tvāṃ rāmarūpeṇa kālaḥ karṣati vānara yena sma vidhavāḥ sarvāḥ kṛtā ekeṣuṇā raṇe
english: It is time itself, in the form of Rāma, that has dragged you away, O monkey — by whose single arrow all these women have been made widows in battle.

sanskrit: imās tās tava rājendravānaryo vallabhāḥ sadā pādair vikṛṣṭam adhvānam āgatāḥ kiṃ na budhyase
english: These beloved monkey-wives of yours, O king of kings, have come a long road trudging on foot — why do you not take notice of them?

sanskrit: taveṣṭā nanu nāmaitā bhāryāś candranibhānanāḥ idānīṃ nekṣase kasmāt sugrīvaṃ plavageśvaram
english: Are these not your beloved wives with faces like the moon? Why do you not look at them now, and why not at Sugrīva, lord of monkeys?

sanskrit: ete hi sacivā rājaṃs tāraprabhṛtayas tava puravāsijanaś cāyaṃ parivāryāsate 'nagha
english: O blameless king, these ministers of yours, led by Tāra, and all these citizens of your city sit gathered around you.

sanskrit: visarjayainān pravalān yathocitam ariṃdama tataḥ krīḍāmahe sarvā vaneṣu madirotkaṭāḥ
english: Dismiss these mighty ones fittingly, O subduer of foes, and then let us all sport in the forests, intoxicated with wine.

sanskrit: evaṃ vilapatīṃ tārāṃ patiśokapariplutām utthāpayanti sma tadā vānaryaḥ śokakarśitāḥ
english: As Tārā lamented thus, overwhelmed with grief for her husband, the female monkeys, themselves wasted with sorrow, raised her up.

sanskrit: sugrīveṇa tataḥ sārdham aṅgadaḥ pitaraṃ rudan citām āropayām āsa śokenābhihatendriyaḥ
english: Then Aṅgada, together with Sugrīva, weeping for his father and his senses struck down by grief, placed Vālī upon the funeral pyre.

sanskrit: tato 'gniṃ vidhivad dattvā so 'pasavyaṃ cakāra ha pitaraṃ dīrgham adhvānaṃ prasthitaṃ vyākulendriyaḥ
english: Then, having duly offered fire, he walked the circumambulation counter-clockwise around his father, who had set out on the long journey — his senses overwhelmed with grief.

sanskrit: saṃskṛtya vālinaṃ te tu vidhipūrvaṃ plavaṃgamāḥ ājagmur udakaṃ kartuṃ nadīṃ śītajalāṃ śubhām
english: Having performed the rites for Vālī according to prescribed custom, those monkeys went to a river of cool, auspicious waters to make the water-offering.

sanskrit: tatas te sahitās tatra aṅgadaṃ sthāpya cāgrataḥ sugrīvatārāsahitāḥ siṣicur vāline jalam
english: There, assembled together, they placed Aṅgada at the fore; and together with Sugrīva and Tārā, they poured the water-oblation for Vālī.

sanskrit: sugrīveṇaiva dīnena dīno bhūtvā mahābalaḥ samānaśokaḥ kākutsthaḥ pretakāryāṇy akārayat
english: And Kākutstha — Rāma of great might — himself stricken, sharing the same grief together with the wretched Sugrīva, caused all the funeral rites to be performed.
